label: rem:phil:craig; sec:limits:textbook; thm:shape:invisible

label: sec:intro:contrib (4); sec:terms:reading
problem: Part (iv) of the dilemma theorem is paraphrased as needing 'objects unlike every named one' or 'objects outside the named structure'. What is proved is only that such a finite theory must prove some {e,s0,s1}-sentence false in the named structure; the sentence ∃z s1s1z=z is specific to the construction (final-check §4 item 8). Whether a unary theoretical function suffices is open (q:terms:unaryfunction).
fix: Intro: '... a finite theory with only unary theoretical predicates and constants, compatible with the theory of the named objects, fits exactly the regular sets; one binary theoretical relation, or a theory that proves something false about the named objects, fits more.' §8.6: 'theoretical entities (for the theory we build, objects outside the named structure)'.

problem: 'version by version (coin-free, one-tape, Kolmogorov), SAI agrees with SOI over consistent labellers up to constant factors': the Kolmogorov versions agree up to additive constants (thm:soi:coinfree(b)).
fix: '... up to constant factors (additive constants for the Kolmogorov versions)' or 'up to constants'.

problem: The third outcome is called 'open'; everywhere else it is 'independent' (label iota), and 'open' otherwise means an open question.
fix: 'three outcomes: proved, refuted, independent'.
